gh pr checks --required lists only contexts that have reported, so counting not-passing over that list settles on an incomplete set and a context that never started reads as absent-and-fine.

evidence_ids: merge-gate.mjs holds every decision as a function over supplied evidence and imports only node:fs and node:url; merge-pr.sh collects evidence and delegates the judgment
evaluateRequiredChecks reads the protected branch required-context list and reports never-reported and not-passing distinctly; the PR #245 shape and its null control are both asserted
selectMergeMethod returns --merge for every pull request, records the archive reason without selecting on it, and refuses a pull request reporting no changed paths
the design-pattern-governance job runs node --test .github/scripts/*.test.mjs, executing merge-gate.test.mjs and the previously unrun npm-audit-retry.test.mjs

security_justification.audit_integrity: Keeps every commit a governance record binds reachable from the branch head by landing every pull request as a merge commit, so check-governance-history can still verify the binding.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: Changes no authentication or authorization surface; the gate reads branch protection and reviewer runs and grants no capability the operator did not already hold.
security_justification.authority_provenance: Binds the review verdict to the exact reviewed head and reads it from run metadata, so a completed run of unknown verdict cannot pass as authority to merge.
security_justification.concurrency: The decision module holds no shared state and each evaluation is independent, so concurrent merge attempts cannot observe one another's intermediate results.
security_justification.confidentiality: Evidence carries pull request metadata, check names, and review verdicts only; no secret, token, or file content enters the evidence object or any diagnostic.
security_justification.cryptography: Introduces no cryptography; commit identity is compared as an opaque string supplied by GitHub, never derived or validated locally.
security_justification.error_disclosure: Diagnostics name the failing gate, the violated class, and the context or verdict at fault, and never echo evidence payloads or command output back to the caller.
security_justification.external_security_integration: Adds no exporter, collector, transport, or SIEM surface; the only external calls remain the gh and hermes reads the operator entry point already performed.
security_justification.fail_posture: Unreadable branch protection, an unparseable check list, an absent review binding, and a pull request with no changed paths each refuse the merge rather than defaulting to permit.
security_justification.lifecycle: The gate runs once per merge attempt and holds no state between attempts; its arms additionally run on every pull request inside the required governance check.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: The only mutation is the merge itself, performed by the operator entry point after a clean gate report; the decision module writes nothing.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: Processes no user payload and no personal data; the evidence object is repository control-plane metadata only.
security_justification.resource_retention: Retains nothing between runs, writes no cache or temporary artifact, and holds evidence only for the lifetime of a single evaluation.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: Evaluation is deterministic and idempotent over the same evidence, so re-running the gate after a transient failure cannot produce a different verdict from the same inputs.
security_justification.trust_boundary: Draws the boundary at the evidence object: everything outside it is untrusted input read from GitHub and Kanban, and the gate treats absence of evidence as refusal rather than consent.
